caption: Figure 2: Visualization of a stack of causal convolutional layers.
description:

Arrows indicate the flow of data from one layer to the next, demonstrating the causal nature of the connections.

caption: Figure 3: Visualization of a stack of dilated causal convolutional layers.
description:
## Index Section 1: Figure Description
This figure is a visualization of a stack of dilated causal convolutional layers, as described in the paper "WaveNet: A Generative Model for Raw Audio." It shows multiple layers of nodes, each representing a neuron, with connections between them. The layers are labeled as "Input," "Hidden Layer Dilation = 1," "Hidden Layer Dilation = 2," "Hidden Layer Dilation = 4," and "Output Dilation = 8." Arrows indicate the flow of information from one layer to the next, with dilation increasing as the layers progress from input to output.

caption: Figure 4: Overview of the residual block and the entire architecture.
description:
Figure type: Architecture diagram
Description: The figure shows the architecture of a residual block within the WaveNet model. It includes a dilated convolution, a tanh activation function, and a sigma function. The output of the dilated convolution is passed through a tanh function, then multiplied by a sigma function, and added to the input of the block. This process is repeated k times, forming k layers. Residual connections are used to add the input to the output of each layer. The final output is passed through a softmax function to produce the final output.

caption: Figure 5: Subjective preference scores (%) of speech samples between (top) two baselines, (middle) two WaveNets, and (bottom) the best baseline and WaveNet. Note that LSTM and Concat correspond to LSTM-RNN-based statistical parametric and HMM-driven unit selection concatenative baseline synthesizers, and WaveNet (L) and WaveNet (L+F) correspond to the WaveNet conditioned on linguistic features only and that conditioned on both linguistic features and log F 0 values.
description:
This figure presents three bar charts comparing preference scores for speech samples between different models. The top chart compares LSTM and Concatenative models, showing LSTM with 23.3% and Concatenative with 63.6% for North American English, and 50.6% and 13.1% for Mandarin Chinese. The middle chart compares WaveNet (L) and WaveNet (L+F), with WaveNet (L) at 17.8% and WaveNet (L+F) at 37.9% for North American English, and 10.0% and 25.5% for Mandarin Chinese. The bottom chart compares the Best baseline and WaveNet (L+F), with the Best baseline at 20.1% and WaveNet (L+F) at 49.3% for North American English, and 12.5% and 29.3% for Mandarin Chinese.

The figure compares the subjective preference scores of speech samples generated by different models, highlighting the performance of WaveNet models over traditional baselines. The preference scores indicate that WaveNet models, especially when conditioned on both linguistic features and log F0 values, are preferred over traditional LSTM and concatenative models, particularly for Mandarin Chinese.

caption: Figure 6: Outline of statistical parametric speech synthesis.
description:
Description: The figure is a diagram outlining the process of statistical parametric speech synthesis. It shows two main stages: training and synthesis. During training, speech and text are analyzed and used to train a model. The trained model is then used in the synthesis stage, where text analysis and feature prediction are performed to generate speech.
